Note::nlp_mask_pii¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note::nlp_mask_pii() const -> Note
Note::nlp_mask_pii(std::int64_t flags) const -> Note

What It Does¶

Masks several classes of personally identifiable or sensitive text-like spans with placeholder markers.

This is one of the most practically useful Note preprocessing methods when you want to keep the sentence structure but neutralize emails, dates, times, currency amounts, mentions, hashtags, and related surface forms before export, modeling, or logging.

The important distinction from deletion-based cleanup is that masking preserves the sentence shell. Downstream code can still see roughly what kind of content was present and where it appeared.

Parameters¶

flags

Optional masking-policy flags.

Use the zero-argument form when you want the library’s default masking policy. Reach for the flagged overload only when you already know the implementation flag contract you want. This page avoids inventing undocumented flag semantics.

Returns¶

Note A shape-preserving Note with supported sensitive spans replaced by placeholder markers.

Examples¶

Example 1. Mask multiple sensitive span classes while preserving the sentence shell.

auto pii = pluss::make_note({
    "Email bob@example.com at 9:30am on 2025-01-03, pay $12.50 to @alice #ops",
    "Backup contact: jane@pluss.dev",
});

auto out = pii.nlp_mask_pii();
std::cout << "nlp_mask_pii:\n";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < out.numel(); ++i) {
  std::cout << "  [" << i << "] " << out.at(i) << "\n";
}

Output¶

nlp_mask_pii:
  [0] Email [EMAIL] at [TIME] on [DATE], pay [CUR] to [MENTION] [HASHTAG]
  [1] Backup contact: [EMAIL]

Example 2. Inspect the masked result when you want to confirm a specific placeholder class was emitted.

auto masked = pluss::make_note({
    "Email bob@example.com at 9:30am on 2025-01-03, pay $12.50 to @alice #ops",
    "Backup contact: jane@pluss.dev",
}).nlp_mask_pii();

auto email_slots = masked.contains("[EMAIL]");
std::cout << "nlp_mask_pii_contains_email:";
for (std::uint8_t v : email_slots) {
  std::cout << " " << static_cast<int>(v);
}
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

nlp_mask_pii_contains_email: 1 1

Notes¶

  • nlp_mask_pii() keeps the sentence skeleton readable while masking detected sensitive fragments.

  • This is usually preferable to full deletion when downstream consumers still benefit from the surrounding context or syntax.

  • If your only goal is link removal, nlp_remove_urls is the smaller and more targeted primitive.

See Also¶

  • Note::nlp_remove_urls: remove only URL-like spans.

  • Note::tokenize_words: tokenize the masked text after cleanup.
